diagnostic_evidence.quote: This source traces a trajectory defined by the continuous function $a(t): [0, T] \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^3$.

issues.failure_explanation: The model defines a(t): [0,T] → R^3 as the spatial trajectory, but the first item of Assumption sump declares 'a(t)∈C([0,T]) is a real-valued function' and simultaneously requires |a'(t)| < c. A real-valued a cannot trace a spatial trajectory, and a merely continuous a need not possess a derivative, so the subluminality condition |a'(t)| < c — the premise used to justify the model and signal separability — is not well defined as stated.

failure_location.quote: $a(t)\in C([0,T])$ is a real-valued function, and $|a'(t)|<c, t\in [0,T]$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reformulate the item as: a ∈ C¹([0,T]; R³) with |a'(t)| < c for t ∈ [0,T], removing 'real-valued'. No other change is needed.
issues.overall_effect: The standing hypothesis of the paper's model is incoherent as written; the subluminality condition on which the physical interpretation and separability discussion rest is not a well-defined requirement.
issues.title: Trajectory assumption is ill-posed: real-valued a(t) with bounded derivative but only continuity assumed
issues.why_classification: A local, forced reformulation of a single hypothesis; every theorem, guarantee, and the advertised scope of the method survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper asserts the second assumption guarantees the pulses remain separable in the recorded signals. From the paper's own far-field expression, the contribution of the pulse at t_j is supported in the arrival window t ∈ [t_j − c⁻¹sup(x̂·D̄_j), t_j − c⁻¹inf(x̂·D̄_j)]. These windows overlap whenever the source moves toward the observation direction: for c = 1, D_j = B_0.1(0.9j·x̂), t_j = j (so |a′| = 0.9 < c and t_j − t_{j−1} = 1 > 0.2 = diam D_{j−1}/c), the windows are [0.1j − 0.1, 0.1j + 0.1], which overlap. Hence the assumption does not ensure separability, the promised rigorous derivation cannot exist, and the extraction of the separated patterns u_j^∞ used in ISP′ and Corollary cor:added-1 is unjustified in this regime.

failure_location.quote: The second assumption ensures that wave signals generated at different instants remain separable due to non-overlapping supports.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the second assumption to require pairwise disjoint arrival windows [t_j − c⁻¹sup(x̂·D̄_j), t_j − c⁻¹inf(x̂·D̄_j)] for the observation directions used, and prove separability from the displayed far-field formula under it.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed separability of the time signals, the reduction of ISP′ to single-pulse problems, and the justification of Corollary cor:added-1's data premise become unreliable for sources moving toward a receiver; the paper's illustrative example works only because the source recedes.
issues.title: Separability of recorded pulses does not follow from the gap assumption
issues.why_classification: A local strengthening of one assumption restores the guarantee; the reconstruction method, its conclusions, and the numerical regime are unaffected.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem RH claims Range(F_#^{1/2}) = Range(L) when |S| > 0 merely a.e. Coercivity of T_# (multiplication by |S|/√(2π)) then fails, so the cited Theorem A.1 does not apply to F directly; the proof instead truncates to D∖Ȳ_ε where coercivity holds, shows ‖𝓕_ε − F‖ → 0, and concludes that the ranges converge. Norm convergence of operators does not imply convergence of ranges (e.g., A_n = n⁻¹I → 0 has Range(A_n) = Y while Range(0) = {0}); 'lim Range' is never defined; and the crucial estimate sup_ε ‖𝓕_{ε,#}^{−1/2}g_ε‖ < ∞, which would legitimize passing g_ε = 𝓕_{ε,#}^{1/2}h_ε → g to a representation g = F_#^{1/2}h, is exactly what the lost coercivity cannot deliver. The same invalid inference is repeated for the discretized operators ('in particular, lim Range(F_{N,#}^{1/2}) = Range(F_#^{1/2})'). The relaxed-positivity range identity is therefore unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State and prove Theorem RH under the strict hypothesis |S| ≥ c > 0 on D̄, where Theorem A.1 applies directly to F = L𝒯L*, and drop the a.e.-positivity claim unless a valid limit argument for the truncated ranges is supplied.
issues.overall_effect: The range identity (RI) connecting the far-field data to Range(L) — the linchpin of every Picard-based indicator and uniqueness statement — is established only under the stronger condition |S| ≥ c > 0; the advertised relaxation of the source class (innovation (iii)) and all results claimed under it are unsupported.
issues.title: Relaxed range identity (Theorem RH) rests on an invalid convergence-of-ranges inference
issues.why_classification: Reverting to the strict-positivity hypothesis restores a correct theorem and the entire program with a contained edit, at the cost of one advertised generalization; no new proof architecture is needed, but a claimed contribution is weakened.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Choose the set $\{y_m\}_{m=1}^{\infty}$ such that $y=y_1$.Then we have $\phi^{(\hat{x})}_{z,\eta} \in $ Range $(L_N)$ for all $N\geq 1$. By Lemma \ref{lem4.1} (ii), it holds that $\phi^{(\hat{x})}_{z,\eta} \in $ Range $(L)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The statement is false. For w ∈ L²(D), Lw(τ) = ∫_D e^{−iτb_y}w(y)dy is the Fourier transform of the push-forward of w·dy under the linear map b; this push-forward is absolutely continuous (coarea), with L¹ density supported in [c⁻¹inf(x̂·D̄) − t₀, c⁻¹sup(x̂·D̄) − t₀], so Lw extends to an entire function vanishing at infinity (Riemann–Lebesgue). Each pointwise test function φ_{z,η} extends to the entire function e^{−iτb_{z,η}} of constant modulus 1. If φ_{z,η} = Lw on (0,K), the two entire functions agree on an interval and hence everywhere, contradicting decay at infinity; thus φ_{z,η} ∉ Range(L) for every z, η, while K_{D,η}^{(x̂)} is nonempty, so the 'if and only if' fails. The proof is also invalid: the forward direction re-chooses the sampling sequence so that y = y₁, infers φ ∈ Range(L_N) for all N, and concludes φ ∈ Range(L) via Lemma lem4.1(ii) — an inference that is false (e^{−iτa₁} ∈ Range(L_N) for every N yet ∉ Range(L)); the backward direction additionally claims supp(𝓕⁻¹Lw) ⊂ the open interval, whereas Lemma supplu yields only the closed interval.

failure_location.quote: For any $\eta \in \R$, there holds $z \in {K}_{D,\eta}^{(\hat{x})}$ if and only if $\phi^{(\hat{x})}_{z,\eta} \in $ Range $(L)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace the pointwise exponential test functions by smeared ones (Fourier transforms of L²-densities concentrated near the level set), restate the strip characterization in a limiting sense, and rebuild the indicator and uniqueness theory of Sections 3–4.
issues.overall_effect: The equivalence between strip membership and Range(L) membership — the core of the multi-frequency factorization method as presented — is false; the indicator functions I_η, W_η, I^{(x̂)} and I(y), the determination of t₀ and of the strips, and the uniqueness results of Section 4 (and the abstract's claims) lose their foundation; with the range identity in force the Picard indicators are identically degenerate.
issues.title: Test-function theorem (lem3.4) is false: exponentials never belong to Range(L)
issues.why_classification: A central theorem is false with an explicit structural obstruction; no comparable pointwise version survives, and repairing it requires a new test-function framework, losing the paper's advertised pointwise-test-function foundation and every result resting on it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The last equality follows from the choice of $\{y_m\} ^{\infty}_{m=1}$ and the fact that $S\in C(\overline{D})$.

issues.failure_explanation: Condition (ii) requires D to be covered, for every N > N₀, by the first N balls of radius |D|/N, where |D| is the volume used as the quadrature weight in F_N. The union of N balls of radius |D|/N has total volume N·(4π/3)(|D|/N)³ = (4π/3)|D|³/N², which is less than |D| for all N > |D|(4π/3)^{1/2}; such a cover of D is therefore impossible for large N, so the admissible sequence {y_m} does not exist and the discretized operators F_N, L_N, X_N are built from an object that cannot be constructed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace (ii) by a satisfiable sampling condition (e.g., the first N points form a covering of D by balls of radius comparable to (|D|/N)^{1/3}, with an asymptotic equidistribution property) and redo the operator-norm estimate for the continuous integrand under it.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed operator-norm convergence F_N → F, the range limits, and Lemma lem4.1(ii) — the discretization machinery of Section 3 — rest on a sampling hypothesis that cannot hold, so those convergence claims are unsupported as written.
issues.title: Sampling condition (ii) on {y_m} is unsatisfiable
issues.why_classification: A contained reformulation of the sampling hypothesis plus a standard quadrature argument restores the intended Riemann-sum convergence; no theorem or guarantee is lost beyond fixing the stated condition.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By the choice of $y_m$, the set $\{e^{-i\tau a_m}: m\geq 1\}$ is dense in $L^2(0,K)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The claimed identity is proved by combining Range(L) = Range(F_#^{1/2}) with 'lim_N Range(F̃_{N,#}^{1/2}) = Range(F_#^{1/2})' and Range(F̃_{N,#}^{1/2}) = Range(L_N). Norm convergence of operators does not imply convergence of ranges, and the 'limit of ranges' is undefined; in fact the identity is false: since L_N is injective onto X_N, Range(F̃_{N,#}^{1/2}) = X_N, the sets X_N are nested with dense union in L²(0,K) (density is asserted in the paper itself), so the set of L²-limits is L²(0,K), strictly larger than Range(L), the proper dense range of a compact operator. Moreover e^{−iτa₁} ∈ Range(L_N) for every N but ∉ Range(L): if e^{−iτa₁} = Lw on (0,K) for some w ∈ L²(D), the entire extension ∫_D e^{−iτ(b_y−a₁)}w(y)dy would coincide with e^{−iτa₁} everywhere, contradicting its decay to 0. Thus the claimed identity fails, and so does the inference 'φ ∈ Range(L_N) for all N ⟹ φ ∈ Range(L)' used in Theorem lem3.4.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the equality by the true (and weaker) density statement that ∪_N Range(L_N) is dense in L²(0,K), and note that this cannot deliver range membership; the intended use of the lemma must be abandoned.
issues.overall_effect: The link Range(L) = lim Range(L_N) is false; the discretization argument for the test-function characterization is unsound, and with it the proof of Theorem lem3.4 and everything downstream.
issues.title: Lemma lem4.1(ii): Range(L) = lim Range(L_N) is false
issues.why_classification: The complete source-supported resolution is a contained weakening of one auxiliary lemma statement (to a density statement); the loss is confined to this lemma, whose intended use is separately reported as false anyway.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: K_{D,\eta}^{(-\hat{x})}:=\{y\in \R^3: \inf(\hat{x}\cdot D)+ ct_0 - c\eta < \hat{x}\cdot y < \sup (\hat{x}\cdot D) +ct_0 -c\eta \}

issues.failure_explanation: The strips K_{D,η}^{(x̂)} and K_{D,η}^{(−x̂)} are, in the coordinate x̂·y, intervals shifted by c(η − t₀) in opposite directions. Their intersection is nonempty iff |c(η − t₀)| < (sup(x̂·D) − inf(x̂·D))/2, so η₁ = t₀ − (sup − inf)/(2c) and η₂ = t₀ + (sup − inf)/(2c). The printed formulas divide by 2 but not by c and are false for c ≠ 1; only the midpoint conclusion t₀ = (η₁ + η₂)/2 survives the correction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the missing factor 1/c, giving η₁ = t₀ − (sup(x̂·D) − inf(x̂·D))/(2c) and η₂ = t₀ + (sup(x̂·D) − inf(x̂·D))/(2c).
issues.overall_effect: The explicit endpoint values in the proof of Theorem Th:max are wrong for general wave speed c; the midpoint determination of t₀ and the indicating behavior are unaffected (the latter modulo the range/test-function defects).
issues.title: Endpoints η₁, η₂ computed without the factor 1/c
issues.why_classification: A single forced local correction of a displayed formula; the theorem's stated conclusions and the reconstruction procedure remain intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: W_{\eta}^{(\hat{x})}(y) = \left\{\begin{aligned}&\mbox{a finite positive number} &, \mbox{ if } y\in K_{D,\eta}^{(\hat{x})} \cap K_{D,\eta}^{(-\hat{x})},

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem Th:kd claims a positivity characterization of the single-direction indicator I^{(x̂)}(y), but its proof appeals only to Theorem Th:factorization, which characterizes the two-direction indicator W_η^{(x̂)}(y) = [I_η^{(x̂)}(y) + I_η^{(−x̂)}(y)]⁻¹. Positivity of W does not imply positivity of I^{(x̂)}; the needed step (finiteness and positivity of the single-direction Picard sum from Theorem lem3.4 together with (RI)) is absent, so the argument supports a different conclusion than the one stated.

failure_location.quote: It is a direct consequence of Theorem \ref{Th:factorization} when $\eta = t_0$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reroute the proof through the single-direction statement: by Theorem lem3.4, the range identity (RI) and Picard's criterion, Σ_n|⟨φ_{y,t₀},ψ_n⟩|²/λ_n < ∞ iff y ∈ K_D^{(x̂)}, and note the Picard sum is strictly positive for a nonzero test function orthogonal to the kernel.
issues.overall_effect: The stated characterization of K_D^{(x̂)} by I^{(x̂)} is not established by the given proof (and, through the defective equivalence in Theorem lem3.4, the statement itself is unreliable).
issues.title: Proof of Theorem Th:kd cites the two-direction indicator W instead of I^{(x̂)}
issues.why_classification: A short, local rerouting of the proof through results the paper already states preserves the claim completely; no new construction is needed (beyond the separately reported defects).
